messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: predictions from misaligned model
parts:
Finn & others,

 Xavier and I have been working on this binomial-binomial model with two misaligned point patterns. The predictions don't quite fit what I'd expect. When I run a 'simple' model, just a single binomial model with only stk.y, my predictions fall within a 0.02 to 0.04 range for fitted values, which corresponds pretty closely to the range of risk in the study population. When I do this double model, however, I get a very narrow prediction that falls in a different range than what I'd expect:

> range(m.prd)

[1] 0.499999999730990 0.499999999778862

> range(sd.prd)

[1] 0.000728774754394849 0.000886545272648484

 

Model hyperparameters:

                        mean        sd 0.025quant  0.5quant 0.975quant      mode

Range for xi.field 1.470e+04 7.679e+03  5305.4759 1.291e+04  3.438e+04 1.012e+04

Stdev for xi.field 4.291e-01 1.259e-01     0.2389 4.098e-01  7.284e-01 3.736e-01

Range for x.field  7.631e+03 1.107e+04   986.0969 4.392e+03  3.415e+04 2.093e+03

Stdev for x.field  1.754e-01 1.144e-01     0.0353 1.500e-01  4.648e-01 9.520e-02

Beta for u.field   1.252e+00 2.055e-01     0.8428 1.254e+00  1.650e+00 1.262e+00

 

Compute corrected stdev for theta[0]: negative 1.202842  positive 0.869014

Compute corrected stdev for theta[1]: negative 0.984359  positive 1.042373

Compute corrected stdev for theta[2]: negative 1.307514  positive 0.679840

Compute corrected stdev for theta[3]: negative 0.760624  positive 0.935674

Compute corrected stdev for theta[4]: negative 0.813922  positive 1.086136



The current version of the script is below:

stk.y <- inla.stack(tag='est.y',
                    data=list(y=cbind(data$result, NA), link=1),
                    A=list(A.y, 1),
                    effects=list(xi.field=1:spde2$n.spde,
                                list(intercept.y = rep(1, 19532))))

stk.x <- inla.stack(data=list(y=cbind(NA, cmv$result), link=2),
                    A = list(A.x, 1),
                    tag ='est.x',
                    effects=list(list(u.field=1:spde2$n.spde,
                                      x.field=1:spde2$n.spde),
                                 list(intercept.x = rep(1, 2223))))
grid$na1<-NA
grid$na2<-NA
NAgrid<-as.matrix(cbind(grid$na1, grid$na2))
stk.p <- inla.stack(tag='prediction',
                         data=list(y=NAgrid, link=1),
                         A=list(A.pred, 1),
                         effects=list(list(xi.field=1:spde2$n.spde),
                         list(intercept = rep(1, length(grid$id)))))

stk <- inla.stack.join(stk.x, stk.y, stk.p)



form_mis <- y ~ -1 +  intercept.x +intercept.y +
  f(xi.field, model=spde2) +
  f(x.field, model=spde2) +
  f(u.field, copy='xi.field', fixed=FALSE)

model_mis <- inla(form_mis, data=inla.stack.data(stk), family=rep('binomial',2),
                  control.predictor=list(compute=FALSE, A=inla.stack.A(stk),
                                         link=inla.stack.data(stk)$link),
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic=TRUE, config=TRUE, cpo = TRUE),
                  verbose = FALSE)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] predictions from misaligned model
parts:
On 6 April 2017 at 13:59, Paul Lantos <paul....@gmail.com> wrote:
> list(intercept.y = rep(1, 19532))))
> list(intercept.x = rep(1, 2223))))
> list(intercept = rep(1, length(grid$id)))))

Your prediction stack doesn't include either intercept.x or
intercept.y, but instead "intercept", which
doesn't appear in the model formula:
> form_mis <- y ~ -1 + intercept.x +intercept.y +

Correcting that might be all that's needed.

Finn

The model seems to have worked. Now I need to understand it ...

The wide intervals for intercept.x and x-range indicate confounding.
You can try imposing an integrate-to-zero constraint on the spde models; make two different spde objects, one for x and one for xi; specify constr = TRUE/FALSE in the inla.spde2.pcmatern calls. See another r-inla group thread where I posted an example of this yesterday.

Finn

The wide intervals for intercept.x and x-range indicate confounding.
You can try imposing an integrate-to-zero constraint on the spde models; make two different spde objects, one for x and one for xi; specify constr = TRUE/FALSE in the inla.spde2.pcmatern calls. See another r-inla group thread where I posted an example of this yesterday.

Finn
